atoms.text: This guide configures the destination bucket for cross-region replication of an application's uploaded documents using the ReplicaFlow job manager. The destination bucket, dr-docs-replica, is in account 444455556666 and has versioning enabled, which replication requires. The source bucket, docs-primary, is in account 111122223333. Before you add the statement, create an IAM role named ReplicaFlowCopyRole in account 111122223333 and attach it to the replication configuration of the source bucket. In the bucket policy of dr-docs-replica, add an Allow statement whose Principal is the ARN of that role, arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ReplicaFlowCopyRole. The statement grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::dr-docs-replica/*. A second statement for the same principal grants s3:GetBucketVersioning and s3:PutBucketVersioning on the bucket ARN itself. After you save the policy, upload a test object to docs-primary and confirm that a replica with the same key and a replicated version ID appears in dr-docs-replica within a few minutes.

This guide configures the destination bucket for cross-region replication of an application's uploaded documents using the ReplicaFlow job manager. The destination bucket, dr-docs-replica, is in account 444455556666 and has versioning enabled, which replication requires. The source bucket, docs-primary, is in account 111122223333. Before you add the statement, enable the replication configuration on the source bucket so that ReplicaFlow acts on its behalf. In the bucket policy of dr-docs-replica, add an Allow statement whose Principal is the service principal replicaflow.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::dr-docs-replica/*, and it includes an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition that matches the docs-primary bucket ARN. A second statement for the same principal and conditions grants s3:GetBucketVersioning and s3:PutBucketVersioning on the bucket ARN itself. After you save the policy, upload a test object to docs-primary and confirm that a replica with the same key and a replicated version ID appears in dr-docs-replica within a few minutes.

This guide describes the bucket policy for storing nightly database snapshot exports produced by the SnapVault scheduler. The target bucket, db-snapshots-archive, receives one compressed export per database under the prefix exports/. The scheduler runs in account 111122223333 and performs its writes using an IAM role named SnapVaultExportRole. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement with the Principal set to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/SnapVaultExportRole. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-archive/exports/*. It also grants s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so that interrupted large exports can be cleaned up. Add a condition requiring the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal aws:kms, so that every snapshot is encrypted on write. Run a manual export from the scheduler console and verify that the object appears under exports/ with the expected size and encryption setting.

This guide describes the bucket policy for storing nightly database snapshot exports produced by the SnapVault scheduler. The target bucket, db-snapshots-archive, receives one compressed export per database under the prefix exports/. The scheduler runs in account 111122223333 and performs its writes using its own service identity. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement with the Principal set to the service principal snapvault.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-archive/exports/*. It also grants s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so that interrupted large exports can be cleaned up. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching the scheduler's job ARN, plus a requirement that the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header equal aws:kms. Run a manual export from the scheduler console and verify that the object appears under exports/ with the expected size and encryption setting.

This guide covers granting a disaster recovery account write access to a compliance archive bucket. The bucket, compliance-archive-dr, lives in the recovery account 777788889999 and holds copies of signed audit records from a primary account, 111122223333. Copies are made by ArchiveMirror, a replication tool that runs continuously and preserves object metadata. Create an IAM role named ArchiveMirrorWriter in account 111122223333 and reference it in the bucket policy. The Allow statement uses Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ArchiveMirrorWriter and grants s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:PutObjectRetention on arn:aws:s3:::compliance-archive-dr/records/*. Add a condition that requires the s3:x-amz-acl header to equal bucket-owner-full-control, so that the recovery account owns every copy. Because Object Lock is enabled on the bucket, the copies retain the retention period set by the tool. Verify the configuration by writing a test record and checking that its retention mode matches the primary copy.

This guide covers granting a disaster recovery account write access to a compliance archive bucket. The bucket, compliance-archive-dr, lives in the recovery account 777788889999 and holds copies of signed audit records from a primary account, 111122223333. Copies are made by ArchiveMirror, a replication tool that runs continuously and preserves object metadata. Reference the tool's service identity in the bucket policy instead of a customer-managed identity. The Allow statement uses Principal archivemirror.amazonaws.com and grants s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:PutObjectRetention on arn:aws:s3:::compliance-archive-dr/records/*. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching the mirror job ARN, and require the s3:x-amz-acl header to equal bucket-owner-full-control so that the recovery account owns every copy. Because Object Lock is enabled on the bucket, the copies retain the retention period set by the tool. Verify the configuration by writing a test record and checking that its retention mode matches the primary copy.

This guide explains how to let a virtual machine backup job write image archives to a vault bucket. The bucket, vm-image-vault, stores incremental disk images under the prefix images/ and is owned by account 111122223333. The backup agent, DiskKeep, is installed on the hosts and uploads chunks with multipart uploads. DiskKeep assumes an IAM role named DiskKeepUploader to perform these uploads. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/DiskKeepUploader. The statement grants s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::vm-image-vault/images/*. Add a Deny statement for the same principal on s3:DeleteObject so that a compromised host cannot remove existing images. Start a full backup of a test host and confirm that the image chunks and the manifest file are present under images/.

This guide explains how to let a virtual machine backup job write image archives to a vault bucket. The bucket, vm-image-vault, stores incremental disk images under the prefix images/ and is owned by account 111122223333. The backup service, DiskKeep, is managed centrally and uploads chunks with multipart uploads. DiskKeep performs these uploads using its own service identity rather than a customer role. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement whose Principal is diskkeep.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::vm-image-vault/images/*, restricted by an aws:SourceAccount condition of 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the DiskKeep backup plan. Add a Deny statement for the same service principal on s3:DeleteObject so that a misconfigured plan cannot remove existing images. Start a full backup of a test host and confirm that the image chunks and the manifest file are present under images/.

This guide sets up a secondary copy of audit logs for durability. The primary log bucket, audit-logs-primary, is in account 111122223333, and the copy is written to audit-logs-secondary in account 222233334444 in another region. A copy task from the LogTwin utility reads new objects from the primary bucket and writes them to the secondary bucket every five minutes. The task runs under an IAM role named LogTwinCopyRole in account 111122223333. In the bucket policy of audit-logs-secondary, add an Allow statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/LogTwinCopyRole. The statement grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audit-logs-secondary/copied/* and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN. Add a condition that the s3:x-amz-storage-class header equal STANDARD_IA to reduce storage cost for the copies. Write a sample log file to the primary bucket and confirm that it appears under copied/ in the secondary bucket after the next cycle.

This guide sets up a secondary copy of audit logs for durability. The primary log bucket, audit-logs-primary, is in account 111122223333, and the copy is written to audit-logs-secondary in account 222233334444 in another region. A copy task from the LogTwin service reads new objects from the primary bucket and writes them to the secondary bucket every five minutes. The task executes under the service's own identity. In the bucket policy of audit-logs-secondary, add an Allow statement with Principal logtwin.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audit-logs-secondary/copied/* and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN, and is limited by aws:SourceAccount 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the copy task. Add a condition that the s3:x-amz-storage-class header equal STANDARD_IA to reduce storage cost for the copies. Write a sample log file to the primary bucket and confirm that it appears under copied/ in the secondary bucket after the next cycle.

This guide covers read access to a source bucket for a continuous backup job. The bucket, orders-media, in account 111122223333 holds product images that are backed up to a separate vault bucket. The backup job, BucketKeep, lists the source bucket and reads each new or changed object. BucketKeep uses an IAM role named BucketKeepReader that is defined in the backup account 555566667777. In the bucket policy of orders-media, add an Allow statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/BucketKeepReader. The statement grants s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::orders-media/* and s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketVersioning on the bucket ARN. No write or delete actions are included, so the source data cannot be altered by the backup job. After saving, start a baseline backup and confirm that the object count in the vault matches the count in orders-media.

This guide covers read access to a source bucket for a continuous backup job. The bucket, orders-media, in account 111122223333 holds product images that are backed up to a separate vault bucket. The backup job, BucketKeep, lists the source bucket and reads each new or changed object. BucketKeep reads using its own service identity, operating on behalf of the backup account 555566667777. In the bucket policy of orders-media, add an Allow statement with Principal bucketkeep.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion onarn:aws:s3:::orders-media/* and s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketVersioning on the bucket ARN, restricted by aws:SourceAccount 555566667777 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the backup plan. No write or delete actions are included, so the source data cannot be altered by the backup job. After saving, start a baseline backup and confirm that the object count in the vault matches the count in orders-media.

This guide describes how to allow a restore workflow to read objects from a backup bucket into a recovery region. The backup bucket, retail-backup-vault, in account 111122223333 contains point-in-time copies under the prefix daily/. The restore workflow, RestoreRunner, retrieves the selected copies and writes them to a recovery bucket in another region. The workflow's reads are authorized through an IAM role named RestoreRunnerRole in account 888899990000. In the bucket policy of retail-backup-vault, add an Allow statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/RestoreRunnerRole. The statement grants s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::retail-backup-vault/daily/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of daily/*. Archived objects must be restored to an accessible tier first, so the statement also grants s3:RestoreObject. Run a restore of one daily copy and compare checksums of the restored objects with those in the vault.

This guide describes how to allow a restore workflow to read objects from a backup bucket into a recovery region. The backup bucket, retail-backup-vault, in account 111122223333 contains point-in-time copies under the prefix daily/. The restore workflow, RestoreRunner, retrieves the selected copies and writes them to a recovery bucket in another region. The workflow's reads are authorized through its own service identity. In the bucket policy of retail-backup-vault, add an Allow statement with Principal restorerunner.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::retail-backup-vault/daily/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of daily/*. Archived objects must be restored to an accessible tier first, so the statement also grants s3:RestoreObject, and every grant is limited by aws:SourceAccount 888899990000 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the restore workflow. Run a restore of one daily copy and compare checksums of the restored objects with those in the vault.

This guide configures a warm standby bucket that is populated by a batch copy based on a bucket inventory. The standby bucket, catalog-standby, in account 111122223333 receives copies of catalog files listed in a daily inventory report from the production bucket. The batch tool, InventoryCopier, reads the inventory manifest and issues one copy request for each listed object. These requests are made by an IAM role named InventoryCopierRole in account 999900001111. In the bucket policy of catalog-standby, add an Allow statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/InventoryCopierRole. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-standby/catalog/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. A separate statement for the same role grants s3:GetObject on the bucket that stores the inventory reports, inventory-reports-prod, under the prefix manifests/. Trigger a batch run and confirm that the completion report shows zero failed copy requests.

This guide configures a warm standby bucket that is populated by a batch copy based on a bucket inventory. The standby bucket, catalog-standby, in account 111122223333 receives copies of catalog files listed in a daily inventory report from the production bucket. The batch service, InventoryCopier, reads the inventory manifest and issues one copy request for each listed object. These requests are made under the service's own identity. In the bucket policy of catalog-standby, add an Allow statement with Principal inventorycopier.amazonaws.com. The statement grants s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-standby/catalog/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted by aws:SourceAccount 999900001111 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the batch job. A separate statement for the same service principal grants s3:GetObject on the bucket that stores the inventory reports, inventory-reports-prod, under the prefix manifests/. Trigger a batch run and confirm that the completion report shows zero failed copy requests.
